question.text: An organic compound [A], molecular formula <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>10</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>20</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> was hydrolyzed with dilute sulphuric acid to given a carboxylic acid [B] and an alcohol [C]. Oxidation of [C] with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CrO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> produced [B]. Which of the following structures are not possible for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>[</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>]</mo></math>
